title: The Rope Crossing
logline: At a hand-pulled crossing, passengers take hold of a rope and arrive on the far side under their own weight, carrying nothing of the bank they left, and yet without that bank they could not have crossed at all.
human_question: When something continues, what exactly is it that continues?

situation.what_happens: A hand-pulled crossing works all day, taking people, goods and bicycles over water that has no bridge. The person working the rope repeats the same short journey dozens of times. Nothing physically travels from one side to the other except the people and what they carry; the bank they push off from stays where it is, and they land on the far side under their own weight.
situation.who_is_involved: The person who works the crossing and is paid per trip or per day; the people who cross every day for work, school or market and who have no alternative; and the households on both sides whose lives are shaped by how long the crossing takes.
situation.what_is_at_stake: A livelihood that ends the day a bridge is built, and a community's access to everything on the other side.
situation.how_it_unfolds: A crossing like this runs in a repeated daily rhythm and ends, over years, either by being replaced or by being abandoned when the people who used it move away. Whether any such crossing is still operating is the first thing reality decides.

concept_merge.why_together: C080 supplies the source's own image for rebirth-linking: a man crossing a stream on a rope tied to a tree on the near bank, who lands by his own weight and brings nothing of that bank with him. C081 supplies the frame around it, the methods of identity and diversity that together deny both an unchanging traveller and an unrelated new thing. A crossing is the simile itself as ordinary work.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: It makes literal what the texts say about continuity without transfer: dependence complete, transfer none.

concept_links.why: The Pradeepika explains rebirth-linking with a man crossing a stream on a rope tied to a tree on the near bank, landing by his own weight, with nothing of the near bank coming across; a hand-pulled crossing is that image directly.

The methods of identity and diversity together rule out both a fixed traveller and an unconnected new thing, which is what a crossing shows: the far bank is not the near bank, and the crossing depended wholly on the near bank.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Something can depend entirely on what came before it without anything travelling across from it.
what_must_be_real: Whether such a crossing still operates at all, the real livelihood of the person who works it, and the community's real dependence on it.
position_hint: middle: it belongs with the group's films about continuity across time rather than support at one moment.
risks: Literalising the doctrine onto the crossing and losing the person who works it.
Building a film on a simile so exact that the people in it become illustration.
drop_if: No such crossing is still operating.

connections.note: Its C080 grounding and its subject, continuity with nothing carried across, are folded into the roof renewal, where the same point is carried by a craft and a household rather than by a simile enacted.

selection.reason: Merged into IDEA-0159, which now carries C080 as a primary link through the skill passed hand to hand; the crossing depended on a simile being acted out in front of the camera.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
